info.name: RepairFlow Backend
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the current RepairFlow Sprint 1 backend. Covers health check, customer registration + email OTP + resend, customer login + OTP + resend, HttpOnly cookie session, refresh-token rotation, logout, protected /me, validation/security tests, and no-cookie/session checks.

IMPORTANT OTP TESTING:
1) Set testEmail to a real email address you can receive mail at.
2) POST /api/auth/register creates a REGISTER record in MongoDB collection `otp` and emails the same 6-digit code.
3) Copy that OTP into collection variable registrationOtp before Verify Registration OTP.
4) POST /api/auth/login creates a LOGIN record in `otp`; copy it into loginOtp before Verify Login OTP.
5) Resend endpoints have a default 60-second cooldown. Wait before running them.
6) Postman automatically maintains the HttpOnly cookies returned after login OTP verification.
7) Do not expect access/refresh tokens in the JSON body; they are intentionally stored as HttpOnly cookies.

item.name: Setup & Health

exec: pm.test('Service name is RepairFlow API', () => pm.expect(data.service).to.eql('RepairFlow API'));

request.description: Confirms that the RepairFlow API process is running.

item.description: Run this first after `npm run dev`.

item.name: Customer Registration

request.description: Creates or updates an UNVERIFIED customer and creates a REGISTER OTP in MongoDB collection `otp`. The same OTP is sent by email. Expected: 202. After this request, open MongoDB Atlas -> repairflow -> otp or check the email and copy the 6-digit code into collection variable `registrationOtp`.

Replaces the current REGISTER OTP with a new code in the separate `otp` collection and sends the new code by email. Default cooldown is 60 seconds. Wait until the cooldown has passed before running this request. Then update `registrationOtp` with the NEW code.
Verifies the REGISTER OTP from MongoDB/email. On success the OTP document is deleted and the user's `isEmailVerified` becomes true. Expected: 201.

item.description: Happy-path registration. If this email is already verified, change `testEmail` to another real address before rerunning.

item.name: Customer Login & Logout

request.description: Checks customer email/password first. If valid and registration is verified, creates a LOGIN OTP in `otp` and emails it. Expected: 202. Copy the LOGIN code into `loginOtp`.
Requires an existing pending LOGIN OTP. Default resend cooldown is 60 seconds. After success, replace `loginOtp` with the newly generated code.
Verifies the LOGIN OTP. On success the LOGIN OTP record is deleted, a server-side session is created, and access/refresh JWTs are returned only as HttpOnly cookies. Expected: 200.
Protected request. Postman should automatically send the access HttpOnly cookie set by Verify Login OTP.
Uses the HttpOnly refresh cookie. Rotates both refresh and access tokens and updates the stored refresh-token hash for the same server-side session. Expected: 200.

exec:
pm.test('Status is 200', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('User still authenticated', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().user.isEmailVerified).to.eql(true));

request.description: Confirms the newly rotated access-token cookie still authenticates correctly.

exec:
pm.test('Status is 200', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('Logout message is correct', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Logged out successfully'));

request.description: Removes the current session from the user's activeSessions array and clears both auth cookies. Logout is idempotent. Expected: 200.
Confirms the session/cookies can no longer access a protected route after logout. Expected: 401.

item.description: Happy-path login plus complete JWT HttpOnly-cookie lifecycle.

item.name: Customer Forgot Password

request.description: Starts password recovery for a verified customer. Expected: 200. For account-enumeration protection, the response is generic. For a real verified customer, check email or MongoDB -> repairflow -> otp -> purpose FORGOT_PASSWORD, then copy the 6-digit OTP to collection variable `forgotPasswordOtp`.

Wait for OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (default 60 seconds) after the previous OTP send, then run this request. Expected after cooldown: 200. The old password-reset OTP is replaced. Copy the NEW OTP from email/MongoDB into `forgotPasswordOtp` before verifying.

Verifies the FORGOT_PASSWORD OTP. Expected: 200. The API returns a short-lived resetToken, and this request automatically saves it to the collection variable `resetToken`. The OTP document is deleted after successful verification.

Changes the password using the resetToken produced by the previous request. Expected: 200. Minimum password length is 12 characters. A successful reset revokes all existing customer sessions and makes the reset token unusable again.

item.description: Complete forgot-password flow. Use a verified customer account. OTP is stored in MongoDB `otp` collection with purpose `FORGOT_PASSWORD` and is also emailed. The verify request automatically saves the returned resetToken into the collection variable `resetToken`.

item.name: Owner Staff Setup

exec:
pm.test('Status is 202',()=>pm.response.to.have.status(202));
const d=pm.response.json(); pm.test('Role is owner_staff',()=>pm.expect(d.account.role).to.eql('owner_staff')); pm.test('OTP required',()=>pm.expect(d.requiresOtp).to.eql(true));

request.description: Requires header x-owner-setup-key. Creates the only owner_staff account as pending and emails an OTP.
Wait for the OTP cooldown, then replace ownerSetupOtp with the NEW code from email/MongoDB.
Activates the one Owner/Staff account.
Validates credentials and sends OWNER_STAFF_LOGIN OTP.
Requires an existing pending owner login OTP and cooldown.
Creates Owner/Staff session using HttpOnly cookies.
Protected Owner/Staff profile endpoint.
Rotates Owner/Staff access and refresh HttpOnly cookies.

item.description: Run Owner/Staff Setup only once on a fresh database. After the first setup request creates the pending owner_staff account, use resend/verify; a second setup request is rejected. Login and session tokens use HttpOnly cookies.

item.description: Backend-first QA for Jira SCRUM-9. Prerequisites: customer registration + email verification completed; Owner/Staff login + OTP verification completed so the normal baseUrl host has valid Owner/Staff HttpOnly cookies.

request.description: Returns job, completed diagnosis when available, eligibility reasons and any already-issued version 1.
Success prerequisite: job status Diagnosing + completed diagnosis + no previously issued estimate.

exec:
pm.test('Status is 200',()=>pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const d=pm.response.json(); pm.test('Current immutable estimate returned',()=>{pm.expect(d.currentEstimate.versionNumber).to.eql(1); pm.expect(d.currentEstimate.isImmutable).to.eql(true);}); pm.test('No longer eligible for another v1',()=>pm.expect(d.eligibility.eligible).to.eql(false));

request.description: Confirms persisted version 1 and Awaiting Approval workflow state.

item.name: Customer - Estimate Decision Copy

request.description: Allows the job customer to view estimate items, version, total, and current status.
Customer confirms approval of the initial estimate. Changes job status to Approved and estimate status to Approved.
Retrying the exact same decision request returns the saved result without duplicate database events.

exec: pm.test('Job status is Estimate Rejected', () => pm.expect(d.jobStatus).to.eql('Estimate Rejected'));

request.description: Customer confirms rejection of the estimate. Changes job status to Estimate Rejected and estimate status to Rejected.
Submitting a conflicting decision on an estimate that was already decided or superseded returns 409 State Conflict.

item.description: Customer estimate approval and rejection requests, including idempotency replays and stale state checks.

item.name: Technician - Assigned Jobs (SCRUM-41) Copy

exec: console.log('No jobs assigned yet. Set assignedTechnician in MongoDB Atlas.');

request.description: Returns 200 with all jobs assigned to the logged-in technician, sorted newest-first. Returns count:0 and empty jobs array when none assigned (informative empty state). Requires technician session cookie.
Full detail view using human-readable reference (e.g. RF-20260923-ABCD). Run after List My Assigned Jobs which auto-saves the variable, or set technicianJobReference manually.

item.name: [SCRUM-41] Get My Job by MongoDB ID

request.description: Same detail endpoint but using MongoDB _id. Both human reference and ObjectId are accepted by the route.

item.name: [SCRUM-41] Get Job Assigned to Another Technician - Expect 403

request.description: Uses repairJobReference (a job created via the Repair Job Registration flow - NOT assigned to this technician). Expects 403. Verifies that no job details are leaked in the error body.
No cookie sent. Uses 127.0.0.1 (noCookieBaseUrl) so Postman does not auto-attach the localhost cookie jar. Expects 401 Authentication required.

item.name: [SCRUM-41] Customer Token on Technician Route - Expect 403

request.description: Send while logged in as a Customer (cookie from customer login flow). Expects 403 - RBAC blocks non-technician roles from the technician job list.

item.description:
SCRUM-41: A technician can only see and open jobs explicitly assigned to them.

Setup:
1. Log in as a technician via POST /api/technician/auth/login then verify OTP.
2. Assign at least one RepairJob to this technician in MongoDB Atlas (set assignedTechnician to this user _id).
3. The list test auto-saves technicianJobReference and technicianJobId from the first result.

item.name: Customer - Current Estimate View (SCRUM-15) Copy

exec: pm.test('Staff/private identifiers are scrubbed', () => { const body = JSON.stringify(d); ['issuedBy','createdBy','decidedBy','customerSnapshot','assignedTechnician','reportedFault'].forEach((field) => pm.expect(body).to.not.include('\"' + field + '\"')); });

request.description: Customer-only endpoint for the latest issued estimate. Expected: 200. The DTO is intentionally scrubbed of diagnosis/internal staff data.
Set customerJobWithoutEstimateReference to a repair job owned by the logged-in customer that has no estimate. Expected: 200 with hasEstimate=false and an informative message.

item.name: Another Customer Job - Must Not Leak

request.description: Set otherCustomerJobReference to a job owned by a different customer. Expected: 404 so the API does not disclose whether another customer record exists.
Uses 127.0.0.1 via noCookieBaseUrl so localhost auth cookies are not sent. Expected: 401.

item.name: Legacy Staff Estimate Context - Customer Must Fail

exec: pm.test('Staff-only context is blocked for customer', () => pm.expect(d.message).to.be.a('string'));
pm.test('No staff/diagnosis payload is returned', () => { const body = JSON.stringify(d).toLowerCase(); pm.expect(body).to.not.include('diagnosis'); pm.expect(d).to.not.have.property('estimate'); });

request.description: SCRUM-15 hardening check. The old estimate-context endpoint is staff-only because it can include diagnosis context. With a customer session this must return 403; customers use /api/customer/jobs/:id/current-estimate instead.

item.description: SCRUM-15 verification for the customer current-estimate view. Prerequisites: 1) the customer is logged in on {{baseUrl}} and has completed login OTP verification, 2) {{repairJobReference}} belongs to that same customer and has an issued estimate, 3) for the waiting-state test, set {{customerJobWithoutEstimateReference}} to a job owned by the same customer with no issued estimate, 4) for the ownership test, set {{otherCustomerJobReference}} to a job owned by a different customer. The endpoint must never return diagnosis/internal-note data.
